title: Personal data sheet; name and birthplace
description: Interviewer Connie Richard fills out a data sheet with Claudine Atkinson, confirming her name spelling, Potlatch address, maiden name Davis, June 7, 1923 birth date, and lifelong residence in Potlatch, Idaho.

title: Parents and siblings
description: Atkinson gives background on her mother Ethredge, a homemaker born in Oregon, and her father Claude, who worked for the Potlatch railroad; both died in the mid-1960s. She names her five siblings and notes most live near Spokane.

title: Marriage to Glen; children and schooling
description: She describes her 1941 marriage to logger Glen Atkinson at her brother's house, her three grown children and their jobs, her high school education in Potlatch, and learning that she runs the machine repair shop.

title: Work history; hobbies and clubs
description: Atkinson says the repair shop has been her lifelong work besides early waitressing, noting few job options existed for local women. She describes bowling in a league, gardening, camping with her husband, and belonging to the VFW Auxiliary.

title: Childhood gender roles; family activities
description: She reflects on girls doing house chores while boys worked outside, says she was not encouraged toward higher education, and recalls camping, boating, and school sports trips with her own family.

title: Courtship and marriage; wartime separation
description: She recounts courting Glen for years, marrying in 1941, and living with her parents while he served overseas. She recalls dancing and movies in Potlatch and how car ownership changed entertainment habits.

title: Marriage adjustment; childbearing decisions
description: Atkinson says the first year of marriage required adjustment but she has been happy since. She and Glen wanted no more than three children, and she describes giving birth in a hospital and a local private nursing home with natural childbirth and ten days of prescribed bed rest.

title: Childbirth changes; hopes for children
description: She notes husbands were not allowed at births and expresses her wish that her children simply be happy without pressure. She discusses her bowling league, recreation with her husband, and how the repair business helped but did not fully support the family.

title: Decision making; logging life; politics; rural preference
description: Atkinson describes her husband making most business decisions, including his move from the chain saw shop to contract logging for Bennetts with long commuting hours. She says both follow politics lightly, she values her life as it was, and she much prefers rural Potlatch to the year she spent in Spokane.
